_doc: Visual system for the VADO technical and financial proposal. Change a value here and every slide follows. Never put wording in this file; wording lives in content.json.

canvas._doc: A3 portrait as PowerPoint stores it: 10.5 x 14 inches. All coordinates in this project are points (1 inch = 72 pt).

fonts._doc: Each alias maps to a Latin face and a complex-script (Arabic) face. PowerPoint needs both set or Arabic falls back to Times New Roman.

digits._doc: GE SS Text maps 0-9 to Arabic-Indic glyphs inside the font, so a plain 402 draws as ٤٠٢. No language tag or paragraph setting can override that: only a different face can. A digit-bearing piece of a run in one of these aliases is redrawn in the alias it maps to. Arabic letters are untouched. Note that in a right-to-left paragraph PowerPoint draws digits with the complex-script face, not the Latin one, which is why the English aliases need recasting too even though Aller itself is fine.

chrome._doc: Page furniture repeated on the content slides (3 to 14). Cover and closing draw their own.

logo_word._doc: The wordmark is a crop of the full lockup, laid over the mark.

rail._doc: Eight squares down the right edge, one per section, so a reader can see the whole document and where they are in it. Every square is drawn: `color` for a section that is in the proposal, `current` for the page being read. The original only painted two of the eight, which read as decoration rather than as a checklist.

cover._doc: Slide 1. The statement block (kicker, headline, subhead, project) hangs from the horizontal rule rather than from the top of the page: it lost the English block that used to sit between it and the rule, and leaving it where it was opened eighty points of white above the rule with nothing in it. Everything below the rule is unchanged.

contents._doc: Slide 2. The numbers sit behind the section names, so they want a tint rather than a colour. Any key from `colors` works here.

contact._doc: Slide 14. The bar under the QR code is unlabelled in the original and its purpose is not recorded; it is kept and named so it can be judged, rather than deleted because it was not understood.

site_map._doc: Slide 4. The old InsertAndPositionPicture macro dropped the map here and then told a human to set transparency to 30% and saturation to 33% by hand. The build sets the transparency itself. The marker is the small square that points at the plot; its position is a fraction of the image, so it moves with the map rather than with the page.

services._doc: Slide 8. Rows are laid out by code: included services first in ink, excluded after in service_off.

phases_page._doc: Slide 9. The tallest the phase rows may be on one page, in points, before the phases split across two. Worked out from the page: the legend may reach 906, it is 15 tall on three lines 17.5 apart, it keeps 14 clear of the table, the table starts at 240.3 and its heading row is 24.8. That leaves 576.9 for the rows. It is one number in one place because the PowerPoint and the browser have to break the page in the same spot, and they measure the rows differently: the PowerPoint has only the heights declared in content.json, while the browser measures what Cairo actually drew.

timeline._doc: Slide 11 Gantt. Weeks are 46.27 pt wide; the grid starts at x_start.

style._doc: Every line and every mark on the Gantt, defined once and named for what it means rather than what colour it is. The chart and the legend read the same entries, so a change here moves both and they cannot drift apart.

capacity._doc: How many paragraphs the main text block on a page can hold before it reaches the footer, keyed by the module that draws it. Slide numbers are no longer fixed, because the scope paginates, so the check reads the manifest build.py writes beside the .pptx. Taken from the box heights the original file had saved, which are PowerPoint's own measurement of that text in the real fonts. A guard against "someone added ten lines", not a ruler.

s06_scope.note: the scope. Paginates, so this is a backstop
